:::{#def-linear-system}
#### Linear system (system of linear equations)

A **linear system** (or **system of linear equations**)
with $m$ equations in $n$ unknowns is an equation
$\matr{A} \vx = \vecf{b}$
in which the $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$ and the vector $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$ are given.
A **solution** of the system is a vector $\vx \in \reals^n$
for which $\matr{A} \vx = \vecf{b}$ holds.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-linear-system}
#### Two equations in two unknowns

By @def-matvec-mult, row $i$ of $\matr{A} \vx = \vecf{b}$ is the equation
$a_{i1} x_1 + \cdots + a_{in} x_n = b_i$.
So the two equations $x_1 + 2 x_2 = 5$ and $3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = 6$
form the linear system
$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \vx = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}$.
The vector $\vx = (-4, 4.5)$ is a solution:

$$
\ba
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 4.5 \end{bmatrix}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd (-4) + 2 \cd 4.5 \\ 3 \cd (-4) + 4 \cd 4.5 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} -4 + 9 \\ -12 + 18 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

The vector $(1, 2)$ is not a solution:
its first equation holds, since $1 + 2 \cd 2 = 5$,
but its second gives $3 \cd 1 + 4 \cd 2 = 11 \ne 6$.

:::
